scope: Visual implementation and reference comparison first; not a new geography-backed training dataset

reference.name: Wildfire Ops generated concept, supplied by user
reference.role: Visual composition reference only; not cartography, operational evidence or a texture layer
targets: High overhead north-up 3D relief with no horizon or sky
Map-filling source imagery with readable terrain contrast
Blue settlement beacons, green refuge and responder symbols, thin leader lines
Orange fire illustrations and a visible downwind smoke column
Single operations panel and thin replay controls below the map

preserved: Engine/reward logic, task configurations and trajectory schemas
True metre coordinates and 1x terrain heights
Existing synthetic population positions and counts, clearly labelled as synthetic
No fabricated fire perimeter, temperatures, burned scar or GPS fixes

terminology.staging_meaning: Simulated responder assembly/departure point, not a verified fire station, incident command post or operations camp

deferred_geography.reason: Match the design before replacing benchmark geography
required: Additional validated heights for the full Sierra Bermeja/coastal outskirts, with explicit land/water/NoData handling
Official settlement footprints, exact label coordinates and dated population inputs
Verified facility access coordinates, separately from assumed staff readiness and live positions
Versioned scenarios and new baselines after relocating populations or response origins

acceptance: Source terrain and simulation inputs still match the frozen v1 manifest
Default 3D framing remains north-up and high overhead at desktop and narrow aspect ratios
Settlement symbols match reference style but are not moved to imitate fictional locations
Controls, replay, uncertainty and source attributions remain readable
Actual browser screenshots compared with reference; mismatches reported explicitly
No commit, push or public publication before user visual approval
